verdict.label: duplicate
verdict.why: Both fetch the environment session state with useEnvironmentQuery(environmentSession.sessionStateAtom(id)), get useEnvironmentPresentation(id), and compose them into resolveFilesystemReadAccess with the same mapping (isCatalogReady, presentation?.connection ?? null, session.data, session.error). NEW inlines the sequence that EXISTING already owns as the useFilesystemReadAccess hook. Because resolveFilesystemReadAccess is shared, only the hook-level composition is duplicated. NEW could call useFilesystemReadAccess(props.environmentId), or the hook could move to a shared package that both apps import. The null environmentId handling is the only variation, and NEW always passes a non-null id. The file tree, query and UI logic in NEW stay in the component.

source_review.counterargument: The approximately ten-line hook wiring could be shared through an injected hook factory. That would introduce runtime/hook indirection while the substantive policy is already shared. Web also accepts null environment and mobile owns file-tree/search/preview behavior; no duplicated permission algorithm remains in these bodies.
source_review.novelty: Pair usefulness only. Repeated endpoints, shared helpers and prior families require root deduplication; no additive novelty/funding claim or provider confidence inference.

scope.negative_scope: Keep platform hooks/composition over the existing client-runtime resolver. A mobile-local convenience hook is possible housekeeping, but does not establish a new shared cross-platform operation in this pair; do not merge the UI component with the web state hook.

source_review.summary: The mobile component and web hook both collect session/presentation data for resolveFilesystemReadAccess, which already owns authorization/readiness/error policy. Their React atom/query/session runtimes belong to different platform modules.
